report.source_text: Patient evolution was favorable, and she was discharged 24 h after the intervention, with phlebotonic medications with diosmin600 mg, one tablet per day, being recommended. The patient was evaluated clinically and paraclinically (blood tests and abdominal and pelvic ultrasound at 7 days and one month). At six months, a control MRI was additionally performed, with no complications being encountered. In order to evaluate the superficial venous network of the lower limbs, a duplex ultrasound was performed. No signs of venous reflux were identified.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Pelvic venous congestion syndrome due to left ovarian vein insufficiency
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old multiparous woman (3 vaginal births) presented with two weeks of worsening diffuse lower abdominal pain localized to the left iliac region, accompanied by slowed intestinal transit and fatigue. Physical examination revealed tenderness and slight muscular defense in the left iliac region. Diagnostic workup began with pelvic MRI demonstrating dilated (7mm), tortuous parauterine vasculature consistent with pelvic varices. Definitive diagnosis was established via venography showing left ovarian vein reflux with dilated caliber (1.1 cm) during Valsalva maneuver, confirming left ovarian vein insufficiency. The patient underwent interventional treatment (implied embolization based on context), with favorable outcome: discharged 24 hours post-procedure on phlebotonic therapy (diosmin), and follow-up imaging at 6 months (control MRI and lower limb duplex ultrasound) showed no complications or venous reflux.
